title.narrative: Community-Based Drug Recovery Services in the Philippines (RenewHealth)

description.narrative: (Philippines): .USAID, through the RenewHealth activity, expands access to quality community-based drug rehabilitation (CBDR) services and voluntary drug demand reduction. In partnership with the Department of Health, Dangerous Drugs Board, Department of Interior and Local Government, Department of Social Welfare and Development, and 32 local government units (LGUs), USAID empowers communities to provide evidence-informed approaches to CBDR services so that persons who use drugs (PWUD) in low to moderate amounts, and their families, can access quality and affordable treatment and care. FY 2022 funds will support the following interventions:.Enhance ability of partners to scale up evidence-based CBDR interventions anchored on the New Client Flow for Wellness and Recovery from Substance Related Issues developed by USAID in FY 2021; Train an additional 5,000 community facilitators and service providers to reach 85 percent of PWUD, screen 80 percent of the PWUD reached, and achieve 80 percent treatment completion for low to moderate PWUD using standard treatment protocols;Sustain partnerships to address aftercare interventions and reintegration of graduated PWUDs to society; Explore setting up systems in workplaces and schools to identify low risk drug users and encourage help seeking behavior for early management; Integrate mental health support for clients and their families; Document models for effective CBDR interventions, and implement customized social behavior change approaches; and.Institutionalize models with the national government and LGUs...USAID works to advance human rights, which is central to the Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance pillar of the Joint Strategic Plan for the State-USAID Framework. Building the capacity of stakeholders at the national and local levels is key to promoting sustainability and achieving the U.S. government objective of resilient and accountable democratic institutions. .. .. .. .
